nodes.title: Pass the open state in as an input
nodes.why: The parent decides which items are open; the child renders isOpen() in its @if and its aria-expanded, so the single-open rule is enforced in one place.
nodes.alternative: Give each FaqItemComponent its own open flag and coordinate the siblings afterwards.
nodes.tradeoff: The child cannot open itself without a parent handling toggle, but every rule about open items lives in AppComponent.

nodes.title: Report a click with a void output
nodes.why: The parent already knows which index it bound, so the event carries no payload; onHeaderClick() only signals that a toggle was requested.
nodes.alternative: Emit the question text or the index from the child, which would then need the index as another input.
nodes.tradeoff: The parent passes the index itself in (toggle)="onItemToggle(i)", which ties the handler to the @for loop.

nodes.title: Leave constant content outside signals
nodes.why: The questions and answers never change, so a readonly array is enough: the @for reads the same reference on every pass, and only state that changes needs a signal.
nodes.alternative: Wrap the content in a signal, or store open flags on the content objects.
nodes.tradeoff: Content that becomes editable or is loaded later would move into a signal so OnPush views see the new array.

nodes.title: Keep open indexes in a signal
nodes.why: One array describes both modes, at most one entry in single-open mode and any subset in multi-open mode, and the template reads it through isItemOpen(i).
nodes.alternative: Store an isOpen boolean on each FAQ object, mixing UI state into the content.
nodes.tradeoff: Index-based state assumes the order never changes; sortable or editable content would key the open state by an id.

nodes.title: Treat open indexes like a set
nodes.why: Multi-open mode adds or removes only the clicked index, with a spread or a filter that hands the signal a new array.
nodes.alternative: Push into or splice the current array, which leaves the signal holding the same reference, so a computed over it never updates.
nodes.tradeoff: Two branches add logic, but they keep the two accordion modes distinct.

nodes.title: Keep one index in single-open mode
nodes.why: Setting the array to just the clicked index closes any other open answer in the same step, and clicking the open item empties it.
nodes.alternative: Append the index and clean up extra open rows later.
nodes.tradeoff: Opening an item closes the previous one immediately, which is the expected accordion behavior in this mode.

nodes.title: Trim to one item when multi-open mode ends
nodes.why: Single-open mode must not start with several answers open; indexes[0] is the item that was opened first, because opening appends.
nodes.alternative: Close every item on the switch, or leave several open until the next click.
nodes.tradeoff: Closing everything would be simpler, but keeping one answer open leaves the reader where they were.
